html:
Pouvanaa a Oopa was a Tahitian politician who led the first movement for self-rule in French Polynesia. He is called the metua, the father, of Tahitian nationalism.

A veteran of the First World War, he founded a party in 1949 and was elected deputy to the French parliament. In 1958 he campaigned for a No vote in France's constitutional referendum, which would have meant independence.

Soon after, he was arrested on charges of plotting to burn Papeete, jailed and exiled to France. With him gone, France went ahead with the nuclear tests. A French court cleared his name in 2018. Later leaders such as Oscar Temaru took up his cause.
